subject: VPC routing rollout caused p95 latency spike — coordination and customer comms
messages:
From: Alex Cortez <acortez@nimbushealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:12:23-07:00
Subject: VPC: sudden p95 latency spike after routing change

Markus / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp jump in p95 for our VPC-hosted calls at ~07:52 PST (spike lasted ~15–25m). Impacted endpoints are /api/v1/generate and /api/v1/stream; tail latency climbed from ~220ms to 1.2s and throughput dropped by ~18%. We've attached a short latency sample and one example request-id (req-20270522-7b2d).

This began right after you announced the routing policy update yesterday evening — wondering if that rollout could have affected our VPC traffic. We rely on low p95 for live triage flows so this is pretty urgent.

Attached: latency-sample-20270522.log

Could you triage and confirm?

—Alex
Alex Cortez
Platform Lead, NimbusHealth
acortez@nimbushealth.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cortez <acortez@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC: sudden p95 latency spike after routing change

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the sample. We're pulling triage on this now. Initial ask: can you confirm whether the 07:52 requests are all from a small set of client IPs or spread across your fleet? Any recent customer-side changes would be helpful but we won't assume that first.

Quick plan:
- SRE (Hiro / Tessa) will verify routing decisions and cache miss/scheduling stats for your VPC.
- If we see the routing policy rollout is responsible, we'll rollback the policy for your VPC and temporarily scale dedicated nodes.
- We'll send a short mutual action plan so everyone is aligned.

I've attached a quick triage checklist I'm asking the team to follow.

Attachments: triage-checklist.txt

I'll coordinate the customer-facing update once we have confirmation (target: within 60–90 minutes).

—Markus
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:05:10-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC: sudden p95 latency spike after routing change

Markus / Marissa,

Quick findings from the serving plane:
- We observed a sharp rise in KV cache miss rate for customer VPCs between 07:48–08:00 PST (miss rate +45%).
- Kernel scheduling queues on a subset of GPU hosts (hostpool-us-west-3b) showed increased wait times coincident with the miss spike.
- Traces indicate an uneven traffic shift: the new region-affinity rule in the recent routing policy rollout is funneling a disproportionate share of NimbusHealth's traffic to 3 pods with smaller token-batching windows, causing both p95 and throughput regression.

Short-term remediation options (recommended order):
1) Immediate rollback of the routing policy change for NimbusHealth's VPC. That will re-enable prior affinity heuristics. (We can do this via the control plane API: PATCH /policies/{id} -> revert to v1.)
2) Temporary bump: add +2 dedicated inference nodes to their VPC for 3–6 hours while we monitor.
3) Enable per-VPC sticky routing override for NimbusHealth (quick feature-flag flip) to force more even distribution.

I can execute #1 and #2 if product signs off on the flag/permission model. If we roll back we need to notify the customer and schedule a follow-up postmortem.

—Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC: sudden p95 latency spike after routing change

Thanks — that's consistent with the rollout telemetry I reviewed. A few product notes and constraints:

- The routing change that shipped last night is gated by the feature-flag vpc_route_enforcement. We can toggle that per-tenant via the console or the internal ops API; toggle requires two approvals for private tenants (to avoid accidental rollbacks).
- We can perform a targeted rollback for NimbusHealth now; it takes ~10–15 minutes to propagate and should restore previous behavior.
- The sticky-routing override Hiro mentions is currently scoped as an emergency-only toggle; we can expose it as a short-term mitigation while we build a proper canary path for private tenants.

Action items I can own:
- Approve the rollback immediately (if Markus approves customer comms).
- Post-incident: prioritize a private-routing canary in the roadmap. I added a short write-up here: https://redwood.company/roadmaps/private-routing-canary — we should scope a Q3 deliverable (design + safe rollout).

If you want me to flip vpc_route_enforcement off for NimbusHealth now, say the word.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Routing & Serving, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cortez <acortez@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T10:00:45-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC: sudden p95 latency spike after routing change

Alex — quick update and concrete next steps (so everything is on one thread):

What we saw: routing rollout last night applied a region-affinity rule that, for your VPC, concentrated traffic on a small set of pods and increased KV cache misses + scheduling waits. That aligns with your observed p95 jump.

Immediate actions we've initiated (in flight):
- We rolled back the routing change for NimbusHealth at 09:25 PST. That should restore previous routing behavior within ~10–15 minutes.
- We provisioned +2 dedicated inference nodes for your VPC (temporary burst) until 14:00 PST today to give headroom during validation.
- We're enabling an emergency sticky-routing override for your tenant for the next 6 hours as an extra safeguard.

Request from you: please upload any additional request-level traces or logs to the shared Drive link (I've included it below). That will help us correlate end-to-end.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_20270522.pdf
Shared logs: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/mk/nimbus-triage-logs

Proposed cadence: 12:30 PST sync (15m) to confirm stabilization; follow-up postmortem tomorrow. If you're available earlier, we can do a 30m window at 11:30.

Apologies for the disruption and we'll keep you updated in this thread.

—Markus
